Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to dull brown velvety spots on upper leaf surfaces that turn corky and brittle over time. Fruit develops scabby dark blemishes.
Apple___Apple_scab.cause: Extended periods of wet leaves in spring temperatures between 13°C and 24°C.
organic_treatment: Spray wettable sulfur or copper soap fungicide before bloom and after rain events.
Apply bio-fungicides containing Bacillus subtilis or Trichoderma harzianum.
Rake and shred or compost fallen apple leaves in autumn to disrupt overwintering.
chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Captan (50 WP) @ 2.5 g/L or Mancozeb (75 WP) @ 2.0 g/L.
Systemic fungicides such as Difenoconazole or Myclobutanil during early active infection.
prevention: Plant scab-resistant cultivars (e.g., Liberty, Prima, Enterprise).
Prune canopies annually to ensure sunlight penetration and rapid leaf drying.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Small purple spots on leaves expanding into circular lesions with light brown centers and dark purple margins ('frogeye' appearance). Causes mummified black fruit rot.
Apple___Black_rot.cause: Enters through bark wounds, fire blight cankers, or insect punctures under humid conditions (20-27°C).
organic_treatment: Prune dead limbs, cankers, and remove all mummified fruit hanging on trees.
Apply liquid copper or lime-sulfur early in the growing season.
chemical_treatment: Apply Thiophanate-methyl combined with Captan starting from petal fall through cover sprays.
prevention: Maintain tree vigor through balanced potassium and nitrogen fertilization.
Prune during dry winter periods and sterilize pruning tools between cuts.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange or reddish-orange circular spots on leaf surface. Underside develops small raised tubular fruiting bodies.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Requires two host plants (Eastern Red Cedar/Juniper and Apple) within a 1-2 mile radius to complete life cycle.
organic_treatment: Remove nearby wild red cedar or ornamental juniper trees where feasible.
Apply sulfur-based preventative sprays starting at pink bud stage.
chemical_treatment: Apply Myclobutanil or Propiconazole at petal fall and continue at 7-10 day intervals during high spore release.
prevention: Select resistant apple varieties (e.g., Freedom, Redfree, Liberty).
Inspect nearby junipers for brown galls and prune them before spring rains.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant green leaves, uniform cellular texture, no discoloration, lesions, or necrosis.
Apple___healthy.cause: Optimal growing conditions, balanced nutrition, and adequate pest protection.
organic_treatment: Continue standard organic compost application and beneficial insect habitat preservation.
prevention: Maintain periodic routine scouting for early pest or pathogen presence.
Ensure proper irrigation and seasonal pruning.

Corn___Common_rust.symptoms: Cinnamon-brown, elongated to oval powdery pustules scattered across both leaf surfaces. Pustules rupture the epidermis releasing powdery spores.
Corn___Common_rust.cause: Cool to moderate temperatures (16-25°C) with high relative humidity (>95%) and prolonged leaf wetness (dew).
organic_treatment: Apply potassium bicarbonate sprays or mineral oil emulsions to reduce spore germination.
Incorporate crop residues deeply immediately after harvest.
chemical_treatment: Apply Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole or Pyraclostrobin when pustules appear on upper leaves before tasseling.
prevention: Plant rust-resistant hybrids featuring Rp1-D or related resistant genes.
Avoid planting susceptible late-season or continuous corn blocks.

Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (2.5 to 15 cm long) developing on leaves. Heavy infection causes leaves to look burned.
Corn___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cause: Moderate temperatures (18-27°C) accompanied by extended overcast days and wet foliage.
organic_treatment: Rotate fields with non-host crops like soybeans or alfalfa.
Shred and chisel-plow residue to bury fungal mycelia.
chemical_treatment: Apply strobilurin and triazole premix fungicides (e.g., Trifloxystrobin + Prothioconazole) at VT to R1 stage.
prevention: Use resistant corn hybrids with Ht genes.
Maintain balanced soil fertility (avoid excessive nitrogen and ensure adequate potassium).

Corn___healthy.symptoms: Uniform deep green leaf blade, intact parallel venation, sturdy stem development.
Corn___healthy.cause: Optimal soil moisture, balanced NPK fertilization, and proper weed management.
organic_treatment: Continue regular foliar seaweed extract or compost tea nourishment.
prevention: Continue monitoring for fall armyworm, stem borer, and moisture stress.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown to black angular spots on older lower leaves displaying concentric target rings. Foliage yellows around spots and eventually withers.
Potato___Early_blight.cause: Alternating wet and dry weather cycles with temperatures around 24-29°C; plant stress during tuber bulking.
organic_treatment: Spray copper hydroxide or copper sulfate pentahydrate at initial lesion detection.
Remove severely spotted lower leaves to reduce inocula.
chemical_treatment: Foliar application of Chlorothalonil (75 WP) @ 2 g/L or Mancozeb @ 2.5 g/L alternating with Boscalid.
prevention: Maintain a 3-4 year crop rotation away from solanaceous crops (tomatoes, eggplants, peppers).
Ensure uniform soil moisture using drip irrigation to avoid foliar wetting.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Irregular water-soaked pale-green to brown lesions rapidly expanding across leaves. In humid mornings, delicate white fuzzy mold appears on leaf undersides. Rot emits pungent odor.
Potato___Late_blight.cause: Cool temperatures (10-20°C) with persistent humidity (>90%) and rain or prolonged fog.
organic_treatment: Spray Bordeaux mixture (1%) or copper octanoate preventatively prior to rain spells.
Destroy and safely bury infected vines immediately to safeguard tubers.
chemical_treatment: Curative/systemic spray with Cymoxanil + Mancozeb, Metalaxyl-M, or Dimethomorph immediately upon local forecast alerts.
prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers.
Destroy cull piles and self-sown potato tubers before planting season.
Hill soil generously around potato hills to prevent spores washing into tubers.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Lush compound leaves, vibrant deep green canopy, absence of water-soaking or necrotized spots.
Potato___healthy.cause: Good soil drainage, certified seed tubers, and timely cultural operations.
organic_treatment: Apply organic humic acid and micro-nutrient foliar spray during vegetative phase.
prevention: Regularly scout underneath dense foliage for early signs of mildew or blight.

Rice___Brown_Spot.symptoms: Small, oval, sesame-seed shaped brown spots with yellow halos across leaf blades. Severe cases cause seedling blight and grain discoloration.
Rice___Brown_Spot.cause: Nutrient-depleted soils (low silicon, potassium, or manganese) combined with high humidity (86-100%) and 16-36°C.
organic_treatment: Treat seeds before sowing with hot water (52-54°C for 10 min) or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/kg seed.
Incorporate green manure and silicon fertilizer to fortify plant cell walls.
chemical_treatment: Seed treatment with Carbendazim (2g/kg) and foliar spray of Tricyclazole (75 WP) @ 0.6 g/L or Propiconazole (25 EC) @ 1 ml/L.
prevention: Ensure balanced soil fertilization with adequate potassium and zinc.
Avoid water stress by maintaining proper field water levels during panicle development.

Rice___Leaf_Blast.symptoms: Spindle-shaped or diamond-shaped lesions with gray-whitish centers and reddish-brown borders. Spots coalesce causing complete drying and burning of leaves.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.cause: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer, prolonged cloudy days, and high relative humidity (>90%) with cool night temperatures (17-20°C).
organic_treatment: Foliar spray of neem seed kernel extract (5%) or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 2.5 kg/ha.
Avoid excessive synthetic nitrogen applications.
chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Tricyclazole (75 WP) @ 0.6 g/L, Isoprothiolane (40 EC) @ 1.5 ml/L, or Kasugamycin @ 2 ml/L at first appearance.
prevention: Plant blast-tolerant rice cultivars suited for your agro-climatic zone.
Apply split doses of nitrogen fertilizer rather than a single heavy application.

Rice___healthy.symptoms: Upright, vibrant green blades, healthy tillering, clean ligules and leaf sheaths.
Rice___healthy.cause: Balanced water ponding, correct fertilizer ratios, and healthy root oxygenation.
organic_treatment: Apply Azospirillum or mycorrhizal biofertilizers to enhance root vigor.
prevention: Maintain continuous shallow flooding (2-5 cm) to suppress weeds and stabilize soil temperature.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark brown, water-soaked circular spots (2-3 mm) on foliage, often surrounded by yellow halos. Margins of leaves may appear ragged or scorched.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.cause: Warm temperatures (24-30°C) with rain splashes, overhead irrigation, and high relative humidity.
organic_treatment: Spray copper octanoate or fixed copper compounds combined with Bacillus amyloliquefaciens.
Prune affected lower leaves during dry afternoons.
chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with copper hydroxide mixed with Mancozeb to overcome bacterial copper resistance, or Streptomycin sulfate where permitted.
prevention: Use certified pathogen-free seeds treated with hot water (50°C for 25 min).
Avoid working in tomato fields when leaves are wet to prevent pathogen transfer.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown to black lesions with characteristic concentric bullseye/target rings starting on oldest bottom leaves. Yellow halo surrounds necrotic tissue; causes defoliation.
Tomato___Early_blight.cause: Warm temperatures (24-29°C) and alternating wet and dry weather; fungal spores splash upward from soil.
organic_treatment: Apply organic bio-fungicide Bacillus subtilis or Trichoderma viride.
Mulch soil around plants with straw or plastic film to prevent soil splash onto leaves.
chemical_treatment: Foliar spray with Chlorothalonil (2 g/L), Mancozeb (2.5 g/L), or Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole.
prevention: Stake and prune tomato vines to keep foliage well above the ground.
Use drip irrigation rather than overhead sprinklers.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, irregular greenish-black water-soaked lesions that turn dark brown and papery. In moist weather, white cottony sporulation appears on leaf undersides; causes rapid plant collapse.
Tomato___Late_blight.cause: Cool, damp weather with temperatures of 15-22°C and high relative humidity (>90%).
organic_treatment: Apply preventative copper sulfate sprays before rain systems move in.
Uproot and immediately bag and destroy infected plants to prevent airborne spore clouds.
chemical_treatment: Apply Mandipropamid, Cymoxanil + Mancozeb, or Metalaxyl immediately upon first signs.
prevention: Grow late blight resistant varieties (e.g., Mountain Magic, Defiant PhR).
Ensure generous plant spacing (60-90 cm) for fast wind drying.

Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.pathogen: Begomovirus (Transmitted by Silverleaf Whitefly Bemisia tabaci)
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Upward curling and cupping of leaf margins, severe yellowing (chlorosis) along leaf margins and veins, stunted bushy growth, flower abortion, and drastic yield drop.
Tomato___Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Vector transmission by Silverleaf Whiteflies feeding on plant sap; rapid spread in warm seasons.
organic_treatment: Install yellow sticky traps (1 trap per 100 sq ft) to monitor and capture adult whiteflies.
Spray cold-pressed neem oil (1-2%) or insecticidal potassium soaps targeting leaf undersides.
Introduce natural predators like Encarsia formosa or lacewings.
chemical_treatment: Foliar application of Imidacloprid (17.8 SL) @ 0.3 ml/L, Acetamiprid, or Thiamethoxam to control whitefly vector population.
prevention: Plant TYLCV-resistant hybrids (e.g., Tycoon, Sakura).
Use fine mesh insect netting (50-mesh) in nursery beds and greenhouses.
Rogue out and destroy infected plants immediately to prevent virus reservoir.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Deep emerald green foliage, crisp leaf margins, vigorous terminal shoot elongation, blossoms setting fruit normally.
Tomato___healthy.cause: Optimal photosynthetic radiation, consistent drip moisture, balanced calcium and nitrogen nutrition.
organic_treatment: Apply dilute seaweed extract and compost tea fortnightly to boost systemic acquired resistance.
prevention: Maintain crop staking, trellising, and suckering for optimal aeration.
Maintain uniform watering to avert blossom end rot and fungal vulnerabilities.
